consequence.statement: ServiceAccount annotation keys and values are now run through the built-in Helm tpl function, so any {{ ... }} template expressions they contain are rendered by Helm instead of being written as literal text.
consequence.remediation: Verify that any ServiceAccount annotation keys or values containing {{ ... }} expressions are intended to be rendered as Helm templates rather than emitted literally.

original.statement: cert-manager 1.17.0 runs the built-in Helm tpl function on ServiceAccount annotation keys and values, so the Helm chart's ServiceAccount annotations now support Helm templating, to aid with workload identity configuration.

decision.reason: [ev-e7cf2f463686] says the chart now runs Helm's built-in `tpl` function on ServiceAccount annotation keys and values. So any `{{ ... }}` text already in those annotations is rendered by Helm rather than written out literally, and nothing in the evidence says this fails, is rejected or stops being honoured. A low-severity behavior-change that needs review is the strongest consequence the evidence supports. Calling it mandatory work would over-claim, and 'none' would hide the change in how annotations are rendered.
